results: pupil examination (size, light reaction): mild anisocoria; the RIGHT pupil is unreactive to dim light, with involuntary pupillary spasms that are irregular in both frequency and duration and unrelated to eye position
ocular motility examination: exotropia, hypotropia and motility impairment - a right oculomotor nerve palsy

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Right chronic oculomotor (third cranial nerve) palsy with aberrant regeneration, most likely congenital in origin

1. Old (remote) traumatic right third nerve palsy with aberrant regeneration
2. Chronic right third nerve palsy due to a previously unrecognized insult (ischaemic, inflammatory, or post-viral) leaving residual aberrant reinnervation
3. Subtle intrinsic midbrain (Edinger–Westphal/subnucleus) lesion not visible on MRI producing a chronic third nerve palsy with disorganised pupillary activity
